Subject: Performance acceptance canvas & operational runbook

Hi Meghan / Avery team,

Thanks again for a productive call today — great context on the peak patterns and the 3rd-party enrichment step. Per our discussion, I captured a concise acceptance canvas below so we can lock scope quickly and kick the POC next week. Please review and confirm or flag edits.

POC objective (4 weeks): Validate that Redwood can meet Avery's production performance and quality goals on your main inference path (document summarization + enrichment).

Success KPIs (proposed):
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end response latency <= 200 ms for a 1k concurrent users simulation (baseline run).
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/sec with sub-200ms median latency; burst handling to 1.2k RPS without catastrophic failure (graceful degradation to cheaper model).
- Cost: average cost <= $0.0008 per token (evaluate token mix with provided workload).
- Quality: evaluation prompt set pass rate >= 90% (customer-provided golden prompts); human-annotated quality score >= 4.2/5 on 200 blind samples.

Measurement plan:
- Week 0 (prep): access + sample workload ingestion (Meghan to share); instrumentation hooks enabled (tracing, token burn, KV cache metrics).
- Week 1: smoke validation on a staging snapshot + baseline perf on small workload.
- Week 2: controlled load test (50% -> 100% -> 200% of expected peak), capture p95/p99, tail latencies, error modes.
- Week 3: quality evaluation (automated prompt set + human review of ~200 responses).
- Week 4: analysis + decision readout (metrics dashboard + replay artifacts).

Owners / roles:
- Redwood PM / Sales: Ben Carter — MAP coordination, demo & readout.
- Redwood Ops / CS: Monica Patel — runbook, on-call rotation for POC, infra config.
- Redwood Eng: Karthik Iyer — perf tuning, quantization & kernel recommendations.
- Avery: Meghan Riley — sample datasets, priority prompt set, approval for load windows.

Immediate asks from Avery (by Fri EOD):
1) Share a representative 24-hour request sample (anonymized) and the priority prompt set (csv).
2) Confirm whether enrichment step can be stubbed during load tests or needs the full external call chain.
3) Approve the week-2 window for load testing (we proposed Tue 21 Jul 09:00-13:00 ET).

Attachments: trial-scope.xlsx (draft timelines), load-profile.json (example), SLA-draft.pdf (rough SLA language).

If this looks good I’ll spin up the private trial environment and send the onboarding checklist.

Thanks,

—

Subject: Re: Performance acceptance canvas & operational runbook

Ben — thanks for the crisp summary, this is close to what we discussed. A few small adjustments from our side:

- Latency: can we target 95th <= 150 ms where possible? Our users are latency-sensitive; if 150 is unrealistic during initial runs, we can accept 200 ms as a fall-back but we'd like to see the trade-off documented.
- Throughput: our realistic steady-state is closer to 250-300 RPS, but we want burst tolerance to ~1k. Please keep the burst target but prioritize steady-state stability.
- Cost: good to estimate token burn; we will provide a breakdown of typical prompt/context sizes.

We will deliver the anonymized 24-hour sample and the priority prompt set by Thurs COB. On the enrichment step — we can stub the 3rd-party lookup for the first two load tests; for the quality run (week 3) we’ll enable the full chain.

Approve the proposed week-2 load window (Tue 21 Jul 09:00-13:00 ET).

Attaching a small sample now (sample_workload.zip) and I’ll share the larger file via secure link tomorrow.

Meghan
